hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: Recent purchase behavior predicts near-future spend: households' spend/basket counts in trailing windows (28/56/84/364 days), average basket value, recency, tenure, and spend trends predict future_spend_4w far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added trailing-window spend/basket aggregates, basket value, recency, tenure, activity flag and trend ratios to the baseline.
reasoning_summary: Future 4-week spend is strongly autocorrelated with recent spending intensity and frequency; windowed aggregates capture level, stability and momentum.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is predicted by longer-run spending levels (8/24/52-week), sequential 4-week block autocorrelation, and behavioral breadth/mix: department-level spend mix, store/product diversity, discount usage, and coupon redemptions — added on top of E001's recent-window aggregates.
transformation_description: Added trailing 8/12/24/52-week spend & basket counts, prior two 4-week blocks, quantity, basket value, recency/tenure/expected-4w, trend ratios, 84-day store/product diversity, discount rate, coupon count, and top-9 department spend mix.
reasoning_summary: Households have persistent spending levels; longer windows and prior blocks give a more stable level estimate than the noisy last-4-week window, and mix/diversity features capture who spends where.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure predicts near-future spend beyond spending history: counts of campaign targets by type and currently-active campaigns, coupon redemptions in trailing windows, and display/mailer exposure of recent purchases add signal to E002.
transformation_description: Added marketing block to E002: TypeA/B/C target counts, active-campaign count, days since last campaign, redemptions 28/84/364d, days since last redemption, trailing-28d display/mailer spend share and mailer letter diversity.
reasoning_summary: Campaign targeting and coupon redemption directly signal upcoming promotions for a household, and display/mailer exposure drives purchase timing, so these should improve on history-only features.

hypothesis: Spending regularity predicts future spend beyond level: a household's basket-count share concentrated on one weekday, weekly spend variability (CV over the last 12 weeks), and number of distinct products over 84 days carry incremental signal about the next 4-week spend on top of the E003 history+marketing features.
transformation_description: Added to E003 a 12-column behavioral-mix block computed over the last 84 days: department spend shares (15), private-brand share, unit price, distinct product count, weekday-shopping entropy, modal-weekday share, count of zero-spend weeks and weekly-spend CV.
reasoning_summary: Regularity/routine features (weekday concentration, weekly cadence, assortment breadth) are known drivers of near-term grocery spend and are largely orthogonal to the spend-level features already in the model.

hypothesis: Behavioral-mix features (department spend shares, private-brand share, unit price, product breadth, day-of-week entropy, week regularity) improve prediction of future 4-week spend when added on top of the full E003 history+marketing feature set.
transformation_description: E003 + 22-column behavioral-mix block over the last 84 days (mix_v1 merged into mkt_v2), no other changes.
reasoning_summary: E004 tested the mix alone and regressed vs E003; the mix may still carry orthogonal signal (regularity, breadth, brand/price posture) that the level/marketing features miss. Testing it as an addition to the full E003 set.

hypothesis: A household's own 4-week spend time series — aligned prior blocks (lag-1..12), the same-season block 364 days back, weekly granularity and block volatility — predicts next-4-week spend beyond trailing windows, with a curated subset (seasonal lags, trend slope, weekly w2/w5) helping and raw block dumps hurting.
transformation_description: E003 + curated 30-feature temporal block: aligned prior 4-week blocks (p1,p2,p3,p5,p6,p11,p12), seasonal lag p13 via seas_ratio/yoy_diff, block counts nb1/2/3/4/5/11/12, weekly w1..w8 (w1,w2,w3,w5,w7,w8), weekly slope, block mean/std/max/cv, trend slope, n_blocks_full.
reasoning_summary: Aligned block history adds information trailing windows miss: the seasonal block 364d back and multi-block trend capture regularity, and weekly granularity captures intra-month timing; offline ridge proxy (fit ≤403, eval 431) improved 65.04→64.57 vs E003 features.

hypothesis: Robust transforms of existing level features reduce tail overshoot and improve MAE: log1p spend levels, per-snapshot winsorized spend levels, and absolute department spends (department share × spend_84, especially gasoline/kiosk which the model overpredicts) added to the E003 feature set.
transformation_description: E003 + 16-column robust-transform block: log1p of spend_28/56/84/364/all and x_exp4w; per-snapshot 99th-percentile winsorized spend_84/28/x_exp4w; absolute department spends (share × spend_84) for gas/kiosk, grocery, produce, meat, drug GM plus log1p of gas and grocery absolutes. No new raw data.
reasoning_summary: Error analysis on a ridge proxy of E003 shows bias concentrated in the top spend decile (pred 505.8 vs y 488.3) and systematic overshoot for gasoline/kiosk-heavy households; log and winsorized transforms temper the tails and absolute department spends give the model scale-aware department signals.

hypothesis: The distribution of a household's own aligned prior 4-week spend blocks (median, IQR, zero-block frequency, max) predicts future 4-week spend beyond trailing levels: MAE-optimal forecasts track the conditional spend distribution, not just its recent level.
transformation_description: E003 (mkt_v2) + 12-column distributional block over aligned prior 4-week blocks: median/mean/std/IQR/max/min of past block spends, zero-block fraction, number of available blocks, current-block-over-median ratio, last-block-zero flag.
reasoning_summary: Distributional statistics of a household's own 4-week spend history (especially zero-block frequency and spread) capture how erratic vs steady its spending is, which should improve conditional-median (MAE) predictions; internal ridge proxy improved E003 from 62.13 to 62.03.

hypothesis: Who the household is predicts its near-future spend beyond history and marketing: one-hot encoded demographic codes (age group, classification_2-5, homeowner, kids) plus a has-demographics flag added to E003 improve MAE.
transformation_description: E003 (mkt_v2) + 9-column demographics block: one-hot-able categorical codes for the ~32% of households with demographics, plus d_has_demo indicator; no other changes.
reasoning_summary: Demographics proxy household size/life-stage which drives grocery spend; internal ridge CV showed a small consistent gain (65.13→64.95, 62.82→62.51) when adding one-hot demographics to mkt_v2.

hypothesis: Shopping rhythm, store loyalty and deal-seeking behavior predict near-future spend beyond history, marketing and demographics: inter-basket gaps, active-day share, day-of-week/time regularity, top-store concentration, and discount/coupon intensity over the last 84-112 days.
transformation_description: E009 (e009_demo) + 27-column rhythm/loyalty/deal block (rhythm_v1): gap stats (mean/std/max/p90), active-day share, baskets-per-active-week, DOW entropy & top-DOW share, time-of-day mean/AM share, streak length, zero-basket weeks, top-store spend share/top-2/n-stores/store entropy/top-store spend, discount rate, coupon rate, item & basket deal shares, deal spend.
reasoning_summary: Recency/level features dominate so far; regularity and channel features (how consistently and where a household shops, and how deal-driven it is) should sharpen level estimates for active households and better identify soon-to-lapse ones.

hypothesis: A household's relative position within its snapshot-day cohort (percentile ranks and robust z-scores of spend, basket and recency levels) plus snapshot-level cohort context (cohort median spend, activity rate, cohort size) predicts future 4-week spend beyond the raw levels in E010: ranks are scale-free so the model can learn "high spend relative to peers" instead of absolute dollars, and cohort-level constants let the model adjust for period drift between train and validation snapshots.
transformation_description: E010 (e010_rhythm) + 22-column rank/cohort block computed inside build_features per snapshot: pct-ranks of s28/s84/s364/b28/b84/days28/recency/basket-value/trend, robust z-scores of s28/s84/b28/recency, and cohort constants (median/mean/IQR of s28, active rate, cohort size, median recency, median b28).
reasoning_summary: Ranks remove the dollar scale so the model can key on relative spend level, which transfers across snapshots better than raw dollars; cohort constants give the model explicit drift context. If cross-period scale drift is a real error source, this should beat E010's 62.795.

hypothesis: An embedded self-supervised ridge forecaster — fit at each snapshot on the household's own aligned 4-week spend blocks (predicting each past block from the preceding blocks, recency, basket count, and activity), then applied to the current snapshot — produces a better-calibrated spend prediction than any fixed weighting of lag features, because it learns the optimal lag weighting from ~9-12 in-sample pseudo-snapshots per household rather than from the 12 real training snapshots alone.
transformation_description: E011 (e011_rank) + 7-column embedded-forecaster block computed inside build_features: emb_pred_9/6/12 (ridge fit on pseudo-snapshots k=1..K with 0.9^k decay, 8 design features incl. lag-1..4 spend, baskets, recency, share, activity), emb_sp (spend-only design), emb_clip, emb_ratio, emb_diff.
reasoning_summary: The pilot at day 431 showed the embedded prediction alone achieves MAE 69.1 vs 77.8 for raw s28 and 75.5 for 0.9*s28, i.e. it captures a weighting of lag features the harness model cannot learn from 12 training snapshots; adding it as a feature should transfer that calibration.

hypothesis: Stockpiling and spend-recency shape predict near-future spend beyond levels: a single dominant recent basket (max-basket share of trailing 28/84-day spend), top-2-basket concentration, time since the largest basket, and weekly spend shares (last week / first-3-weeks vs weeks 4-12 of the trailing 84 days) plus a 12-week log-spend slope signal that a household front-loaded purchases and will under-buy in the next 4 weeks.
transformation_description: E011 (e011_rank) + 18-column stockpiling/recency-shape block (stock_v1): max-basket and top-2-basket spend shares over trailing 28/84 days, log max-basket values, days since largest basket and since last purchase, baskets in last 7 days, last-1/2-week spend share of the 28-day total, w1/w3/w4-12 weekly shares of the 84-day total, 12-week log-slope, no-purchase-last-week flag, stockpile flag, max-basket-over-mean ratio.
reasoning_summary: Offline partial correlations on train rows showed max-basket share (-0.20) and weeks-4-12 spend share (-0.18) carry information orthogonal to trailing spend level, so this block should add signal to the level/rhythm/rank features of E011.

hypothesis: Snapshot-level market conditions predict 4-week spend: market-wide per-household spend/frequency indices (trailing 4/12-week, vs 48-week baseline and vs same-phase-last-year), periodic phase encodings with a phase category, year-fraction drift, cohort active share, and the household's own aligned lag-13 (364-day) spend block capture the upward spend drift and annual seasonality that household-only features miss, reducing validation MAE below E013's 62.456.
transformation_description: E013 (e013_stock) + 17-column seasonality block (season_v1): phase_sin/cos + phase category, year_frac, market per-hh spend/basket indices (4w, 12w, vs all, vs prior 48w, same-phase-last-year ratio), cohort active share, household aligned lag-13 spend and its ratio to current 4w spend.
reasoning_summary: Validation snapshots repeat train phases (364-day offset) but the model only saw raw week index; market per-hh spend drifted ~57→66 mirroring train target means 130→146, so market-level indices plus phase encodings should let the model calibrate snapshot-level level shifts.

hypothesis: A minimal trailing-window model (28d spend, 84d spend, 28d basket count, recency, tenure) captures most of the predictable signal; richer blocks add little. This fallback table was produced when the intended flexible-basis build failed inside build_features.
transformation_description: Replaced the entire E013 feature set with 5 basic trailing-window aggregates computed from view.transactions only (the intended hinges/one-hot/department block failed to build because load_saved is unavailable inside build_features).
reasoning_summary: Serves as a sanity-check baseline: if 5 raw aggregates approach E013's MAE, the extra blocks are mostly noise; expected to be clearly worse, quantifying the value of the richer blocks.

hypothesis: Decay-weighted spend (EWMA at multiple half-lives) captures purchase momentum that flat trailing windows miss; a two-part activity×intensity decomposition and kNN peer-profile aggregates add calibration signal for future 4-week spend.
transformation_description: E013 (e013_stock) + 23-column block: EWMA spend at half-lives 7/14/28/56/112d and decay ratios (7/56, 28/112); two-part stats over 13 aligned prior 4-week blocks (activity share, nonzero mean/median/max, pred=act×mean, max/median, last/max, CV, own percentile); k=25 peer-similarity aggregates on a log-spend/recency/tenure profile.
reasoning_summary: Exponentially decayed spend weights the most recent weeks more smoothly than the flat 28d window; separating activity probability from conditional intensity and borrowing from profile-similar peers should calibrate both zero and tail predictions. Internal ridge proxy at snapshot 431 showed +EWMA improves MAE (64.30 vs 64.51).

hypothesis: The fixed model wastes capacity on near-duplicate features: e013 contains many pairwise-|r|>0.95 columns (e.g. 11 near-identical spend-level features, 7 basket-count features), and E017's +12.7 MAE blowup from adding 23 collinear EWMA features suggests redundancy actively hurts. Dropping zero-variance columns and greedy-pruning the highest-|corr-with-target| feature whenever it duplicates an already-kept one (|r|>0.95 on train rows) will improve validation MAE.
transformation_description: E013 (e013_stock) with 30 features removed: 4 zero-variance columns and 26 columns greedily pruned for |r|>0.95 redundancy (ordered by descending |corr| with the target on train rows); all other columns unchanged. 143 -> 113 features.
reasoning_summary: Surrogate diagnostics showed e013 is dominated by large near-duplicate clusters; with a capacity-limited fixed model, removing duplicates should sharpen the fit rather than dilute it, and E017's severe degradation when adding collinear features supports this.

hypothesis: Peer households with similar 84-day department-spend profiles predict a household's near-future spend beyond its own history: similarity-weighted neighbor spend/activity (k=10/5) adds signal not captured by the household's own trailing windows.
transformation_description: E013 (e013_stock) + 12-column kNN-neighbor block (knn_v1): cosine similarity over 84-day department spend vectors; weighted/mean neighbor 28d & 84d spend, 28d basket count, neighbor activity shares, self-vs-neighbor spend ratio, mean neighbor similarity.
reasoning_summary: Similar households tend to have similar spending levels and rhythms; neighbor aggregates act as a shrunk prior that can correct noisy individual trailing-window estimates, especially for low-activity households.

hypothesis: Lull history (consecutive zero 28-day blocks), short-window activity (7/14-day spend and baskets), purchase-cycle phase (recency relative to the household's own inter-purchase gap), and a second level-aware kNN over dept-mix+level+recency profiles predict near-future spend beyond the E019 feature set.
transformation_description: E019 (e019_knn) + 21-column final block: zero-block stats (zb_consec, zb_run_max, zb_frac, zb_zero84), 7/14d spend+baskets+active-days and per-active-day spend + basket-value ratio (b7,b14,s7,s14,days14,spd_day28,bvt28_84), inter-purchase gap mean/median and overdue ratios/flag (gap_mean,gap_med,ovd_ratio,ovd_mratio,ovd_flag), and second kNN (kn2_*) over standardized 84d dept-share + log level + recency profiles (k=25, sim-weighted).
reasoning_summary: The target has heavy mass at low/zero spend and E013/E019 lack explicit lull-history, sub-28-day activity and cycle-phase features; peers matched on level+mix+recency should sharpen the kNN signal that already helped in E019.
